cards.title: UGC hardness of homology localization
cards.formal: Does the Unique Games Conjecture imply that, for every fixed approximation factor c>1, there exists an integer k=k(c)≥2 such that c-approximating 1-Homology Localization over ℤ/kℤ on triangulated 2-manifolds is NP-hard? Given a finite triangulation K and a cycle z∈C₁(K;ℤ/kℤ), the task is to output a homologous cycle z′ of minimum possible support up to factor c: |supp(z′)|≤c·OPT(K,z), where OPT(K,z)=min_{u∈C₂(K;ℤ/kℤ)}|supp(z+∂₂u)|. The modulus may depend on c but is fixed before the input triangulation is supplied.
cards.why: Tests whether the strong approximation obstruction associated with Unique Games persists when topological inputs are restricted to genuine surface triangulations. It separates topological equivalence from approximation-preserving representation and connects discrete optimization with the sparsity of homology representatives.
cards.status_note: Read the source’s homology and approximation definitions, Theorems 14 and 19 and Open Question 21 in the conference and full versions. Checked the 2025 paper’s coefficient convention and Theorems 2 and 6. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution of this exact all-constant triangulated-surface target; searches are not exhaustive and the cited proofs were not independently audited.

cards.definitions:
A triangulation is a finite abstract simplicial complex of dimension 2, encoded by a list of vertices, edges and triangles with integer vertex labels and all faces present. Its realization is promised to be a compact 2-manifold without boundary; no bound on genus, number of vertices or number of components is fixed. Equivalently for this finite pure complex, the link of every vertex is a simplicial cycle. No orientability restriction is added. This uses the closed-surface setting of the source’s topological comparison; orientable surfaces are included. Cells with arbitrary polygonal attaching maps are not valid replacements for triangles, and edge weights are all one.

Fix an ordering of vertices and orient each simplex by increasing order. C_d(K;ℤ/kℤ) is the module of coefficient vectors indexed by d-simplices, with all arithmetic modulo k. There is no assumption that k is prime. The boundary of an oriented simplex is ∂[v₀,…,v_d]=∑_{j=0}^d (−1)^j[v₀,…,v̂ⱼ,…,v_d], extended linearly. The input z is an explicit residue vector on the edges with ∂₁z=0. Two such cycles are homologous if z′−z=∂₂u for some 2-chain u, meaning an arbitrary coefficient vector on triangles. The 2-chain need not itself be a cycle. Support is the set of edges with nonzero coefficients; its cost counts each such edge once, independently of the coefficient’s residue. This is the unweighted ℓ₀ support objective, not the sum of coefficient magnitudes, geometric length, minimum enclosing radius or the number of connected components. The minimum exists because there are finitely many 2-chains. A feasible approximation must return an explicit edge vector z′ in the same homology class. If OPT=0, its output must have zero support. No single-loop or connected-output requirement is imposed.

For fixed c and k, polynomial time refers to the binary length of the full triangulation and residue-vector description; the polynomial may depend on those fixed constants. NP-hardness of the approximation search task is understood in the usual oracle-reduction sense: a deterministic polynomial-time procedure can decide 3-SAT with access to an oracle returning any feasible c-approximation, and must work for every valid answer that the oracle could return. Here 3-SAT asks whether a conjunction of clauses with at most three Boolean literals is satisfiable. A promise-gap many-one reduction with separated objective values is in particular sufficient. This fixes the source’s NP-hard interpretation of “hard”; it does not assert a stronger randomized-time lower bound.

A Unique Games instance has a finite graph of variables, a label set [q]={1,…,q}, and for each edge uv a permutation π_uv of [q], explicitly encoded, with the constraint ℓ(v)=π_uv(ℓ(u)). Its value is the maximum fraction of edge constraints satisfied by a labeling. Parallel constraints may be listed separately. The UGC says that for all rational ε,δ>0 with ε+δ<1, some fixed q makes it NP-hard to distinguish value at least 1−ε from value at most δ; intermediate values are outside the promise. Thus the claim’s quantifiers are UGC ⇒ ∀c>1 ∃k≥2 NP-hard(c-approximation at modulus k). Restricting c to rational constants greater than one gives the same all-constant target by monotonicity of approximation guarantees. It does not demand a single modulus that works for all c, and it does not set k=2.
cards.answer_criterion: A positive answer proves the stated conditional NP-hardness for every constant c>1 with a modulus depending only on c, producing valid triangulated surfaces and the specified minimum-support homology task. A negative answer must refute that conditional claim in this model. A result for only one constant factor, general cell decompositions, higher-dimensional manifolds, geometric localization or exact rather than approximate optimization does not settle the all-constant claim.

context_blocks.title: The representative must stay in the same class
context_blocks.text: The optimization changes a cycle by boundaries of 2-chains while preserving its homology class. It seeks a sparse edge-support representative, which may have multiple components and coefficients in a cyclic group larger than ℤ₂.

context_blocks.title: What the source already proves
context_blocks.text: Theorem 14 proves the strong Unique Games equivalence for general cell decompositions of closed orientable surfaces. Theorem 19 gives a 7/6−η inapproximability factor on triangulated surfaces under UGC, with a modulus depending on η. Open Question 21 asks for all constant factors in the triangulated setting.

context_blocks.title: Duality does not preserve every input restriction
context_blocks.text: The source relates homology and cohomology using dual cell decompositions. The dual of a triangulation need not itself be a triangulation. The card therefore retains the stated homology-on-triangulations task rather than treating a cohomology or arbitrary-cell result as automatically equivalent for this objective.

context_blocks.title: Later parameterized results have different scope
context_blocks.text: Blaser and Vågset prove parameterized constant-factor hardness on general simplicial complexes and an exact ETH lower bound on a weighted surface problem over ℤ₂. Their 2025 statements do not provide the all-constant, unweighted triangulated-surface approximation result asked here.

cards.context:
The optimization changes a cycle by boundaries of 2-chains while preserving its homology class. It seeks a sparse edge-support representative, which may have multiple components and coefficients in a cyclic group larger than ℤ₂.

Theorem 14 proves the strong Unique Games equivalence for general cell decompositions of closed orientable surfaces. Theorem 19 gives a 7/6−η inapproximability factor on triangulated surfaces under UGC, with a modulus depending on η. Open Question 21 asks for all constant factors in the triangulated setting.

The source relates homology and cohomology using dual cell decompositions. The dual of a triangulation need not itself be a triangulation. The card therefore retains the stated homology-on-triangulations task rather than treating a cohomology or arbitrary-cell result as automatically equivalent for this objective.

Blaser and Vågset prove parameterized constant-factor hardness on general simplicial complexes and an exact ETH lower bound on a weighted surface problem over ℤ₂. Their 2025 statements do not provide the all-constant, unweighted triangulated-surface approximation result asked here.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
